rules.name: Questionnaire flow overview
rules.statement: The questionnaire has exactly eight steps in this order. Each question is asked once and its answer is reused for every receiving party; a question is only asked when at least one party needs the answer for this person. Answers are saved as the employee goes and they can resume until they submit; submitting needs one confirmation on a summary page.

table.then: Always: first name, last name, date of birth, first working day
Always: street, house number (or 'no house number'), postcode, town and country as on the first working day; canton only if the country is Switzerland
Only employees living in Switzerland: nationality; C permit (yes/no) only if not Swiss

Civil status from everyone; spouse's date of birth if married, registered partnership or separated; spouse's nationality, C permit and whether the spouse lives in Switzerland only for non-Swiss employees without C permit living in Switzerland who are married or in a registered partnership
Only employees living in Liechtenstein or Germany (always subject to source tax): daily return and non-return days; certificate of residence for Germany
Only employees subject to source tax, except Liechtenstein residents in principle not liable: denomination, spouse gainfully employed (married or registered partnership), has children
Only if source tax details are asked and the employee has children: one block per child, no maximum
Always: summary and one confirmation; permit reminder for non-Swiss employees and employees living abroad

rules.name: Insurance start date
rules.statement: The pension fund insurance start date is derived from the first working day only: if the first working day is the 1st of a month, insurance starts that day; otherwise on the 1st of the following month. It is always derived again from the latest first working day.

rules.name: Civil status for the pension fund
rules.statement: The fund only accepts Single, Married, Divorced and Widowed. Registered partnership and Separated are entered as Married (with the spouse's/partner's date of birth); the other values are entered as they are (assumption D-003).

rules.name: Canton for the pension fund
rules.statement: Employees living in Switzerland: the canton they chose. Employees living abroad: the canton of the place of work, Zurich for Muster AG, not asked (assumption D-002).

rules.name: Subject to source tax
rules.statement: An employee living abroad is subject to source tax whatever their nationality. An employee living in Switzerland is subject only if not Swiss, without a C permit, and not married to (or in a registered partnership with) a Swiss national or C-permit holder who lives in Switzerland. Separated counts as single. 'Here' in HR's wording means Switzerland (assumption D-043).
inputs: Spouse Swiss or holds a C permit

rules.name: Liechtenstein resident in principle not liable
rules.statement: An employee living in Liechtenstein who returns daily, or who does not return daily but expects at most 45 non-return days, is in principle not liable to source tax, subject to the double taxation agreement. Lonio shows this instead of a tariff code, flags it for HR and skips the remaining tariff questions.

rules.statement: For an employee living in Germany the cross-border tariff applies if they return daily and have a certificate of residence ('not yet' counts as no), or if they do not return daily, daily return would be reasonable and they do not expect more than 60 non-return days. Otherwise the normal tariff applies.

rules.name: Tariff letter
rules.statement: When the cross-border tariff applies, the base letter is replaced: A by L, B by M, C by N, H by P (and G by Q, which cannot occur for onboarding). Otherwise the base letter is used.

rules.name: Full source tax tariff code
rules.statement: Lonio computes the full Zurich tariff code as one text: tariff letter, number of counted children and church-tax suffix (e.g. 'C1Y', 'L0Y'). Not subject to source tax: 'no tariff code'. Liechtenstein resident in principle not liable: 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement', flagged for HR. When answers needed for the code are missing (e.g. after an HR change made new questions apply): 'incomplete - HR must complete'. Always derived again from the latest answers.

letter + number + suffix, e.g. C1Y, N1Y, A0N, H1Y

feature.title: Employee onboarding questionnaire
feature.goal: A new employee of Muster AG answers one English onboarding questionnaire in Lonio. It asks each piece of information once and only when a receiving party needs it for that person. From the answers, Lonio registers the employee with Pensionskasse Muster, decides whether source tax applies and computes the full Zurich source tax tariff code, so that HR has everything it needs.
feature.context: Today HR at Muster AG collects onboarding data itself and enters it for each receiving party. For the pension fund (Pensionskasse Muster), the insurance start date is 'the number one thing'. It depends on the first working day, and that date often changes. The fund also needs the name, date of birth, canton, civil status and, for married employees, the spouse's date of birth. To find the source tax tariff, HR works out who is subject to source tax using its own rule: anyone living abroad, and people living in Switzerland who are not Swiss, have no C permit and are not married to a Swiss national or C-permit holder living in Switzerland. HR then clicks through the Zurich tariff calculator, including the cross-border questions for Germany and Liechtenstein and the detailed questions per child. HR also wants a complete postal address and asks non-Swiss employees to bring their permit. Asking too little blocks a registration, and asking too much collects personal data no party needs (G-01). Lonio replaces this work. The employee answers once in eight fixed steps (D-047), and Lonio works out the insurance start date, the civil status and canton for the fund, whether source tax applies and the full tariff code (D-001). The sources are fictional and are treated as the truth (G-06). AHV data, IT equipment, the badge photo, how data is sent to each party and all HR screens are out of scope (G-03, G-04, D-034).

sections.title: Questionnaire flow overview

stories.title: Show the source tax step only to employees who are subject to source tax

'Here' in HR's wording is read as Switzerland and anyone with Swiss citizenship counts as Swiss. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: HR's consolidated rule is applied as stated.

stories.title: Ask the steps in an order that avoids unneeded questions
stories.i_want: to go through the onboarding questionnaire in eight fixed steps, in English, where each step and question appears only when it applies to me
stories.so_that: I answer only what a receiving party needs for me, and the answers that decide later questions (where I live, nationality, civil status) come first
stories.priority_reason: The step order is the backbone of the questionnaire; without it no registration data is collected (G-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: Eight steps in a fixed order

There is no separate step for the first working day. A step that does not apply to the employee is skipped. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: this step list and order.

acceptance_criteria.title: Steps 1 and 2 are asked of everyone; the canton only of Swiss residents

Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: the address is the one on the first working day and every address field is required.

acceptance_criteria.title: Step 3 only for employees living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has entered the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: step 3 'Nationality and C permit' is reached
acceptance_criteria.then: nationality is asked only of employees living in Switzerland; whether they hold a C permit is asked only if they are not Swiss. Employees living abroad skip step 3.

acceptance_criteria.title: Step 4 civil status from everyone, spouse questions only where needed
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee reaches step 4 'Civil status and spouse'
acceptance_criteria.when: they answer their civil status
acceptance_criteria.then: civil status is required from everyone, wherever they live; the spouse's or registered partner's date of birth is asked of married, registered-partner and separated employees; the spouse's nationality and whether the spouse lives in Switzerland are asked only of non-Swiss employees without a C permit living in Switzerland who are married or in a registered partnership, and the spouse's C permit only if the spouse is not Swiss. acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has entered the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: step 5 'Cross-border commuting' is reached

acceptance_criteria.given: the questionnaire has determined whether the employee is subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: steps 6 'Source tax details' and 7 'Children' are reached
acceptance_criteria.then: step 6 (denomination; whether the spouse is gainfully employed, only for married employees and registered partners; whether there are children) is shown only to employees subject to source tax, except Liechtenstein residents in principle not liable; step 7 (one block per child, no maximum number of children) is shown only when step 6 is shown and the employee has children. acceptance_criteria.title: Step 8 is shown to everyone
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has completed the steps that apply to them
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach the end of the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: step 8 shows the permit reminder where it applies, the summary of all answers and the single confirmation to submit.

acceptance_criteria.title: Answers are saved and the employee can resume

sections.title: Personal details and home address
sections.purpose: Collect the employee's identity and the complete home address that applies on the first working day, plus the canton the pension fund needs.

stories.title: Collect the employee's name and date of birth
stories.i_want: every new employee to give their first name, last name and date of birth in the first step of the onboarding questionnaire ('About you')
stories.so_that: the registration with Pensionskasse Muster can be completed, because these are required fields of the fund's registration form, and HR can identify the employee
stories.priority_reason: The fund's registration form rejects a registration without first name, last name or date of birth ('... is required.'), so missing values block the registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: Name and date of birth are asked of every employee in step 1
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee opens the onboarding questionnaire, wherever they live and whatever their nationality
acceptance_criteria.when: they answer step 1 'About you' (the first of the eight fixed steps; assumption to be verified by a domain expert, D-047)
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for their first name, last name and date of birth, together with the first working day, and each of these answers is required: the employee cannot leave step 1 complete without them

acceptance_criteria.title: Date of birth is a full date and plausible for the first working day
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee enters their date of birth and their first working day
acceptance_criteria.when: the date of birth would make them younger than 14 or older than 100 on the first working day
acceptance_criteria.then: the date of birth is not accepted and the employee is told to correct it; a date of birth that makes them between 14 and 100 years old on the first working day is accepted. Dates are given as day, month and year (DD.MM.YYYY), as the fund's form expects. The age limits are an assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-050).

acceptance_criteria.title: Who receives name and date of birth
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: the answers are recorded
acceptance_criteria.then: first name, last name and date of birth are recorded for the registration with Pensionskasse Muster; first name and last name are also recorded for HR to identify the employee. The date of birth is not recorded for any other purpose.

stories.title: Collect a complete postal home address

stories.priority_reason: HR posts many documents and states the address 'has to be complete'; an incomplete address hampers HR's correspondence but does not block a registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: All address fields are required for every employee
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee reaches step 2 'Home address' (the second of the eight fixed steps, D-047)
acceptance_criteria.when: they enter their home address
acceptance_criteria.then: street, house number, postcode, town and country are required for every employee, wherever they live; the step cannot be completed while one of them is missing. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-049).

acceptance_criteria.title: Addresses without a house number
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's address has no house number
acceptance_criteria.when: they fill in the house number

acceptance_criteria.title: The address that applies on the first working day

acceptance_criteria.when: they enter their home address
acceptance_criteria.then: the questionnaire asks for the address where they will live on their first working day, and that address is recorded, not the current one. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-041).

acceptance_criteria.then: it is recorded for HR as a normal postal address, the way it is written on an envelope; nothing beyond street, house number, postcode, town and country is asked.

acceptance_criteria.title: Country chosen from a fixed country list

acceptance_criteria.when: they choose the country

acceptance_criteria.title: Residence in Switzerland is not asked again
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio needs to know whether the main residence is in Switzerland and, if not, the country of residence (as the Zurich source tax calculator asks)
acceptance_criteria.then: both are taken from the home address country and are not asked again; the country that counts is the one of the address on the first working day (assumption to be verified by a domain expert, D-041).

acceptance_criteria.title: The country of residence decides what is asked about the canton

acceptance_criteria.when: the rest of step 2 'Home address' is shown
acceptance_criteria.then: an employee living in Switzerland is asked for the canton of residence; an employee living in any other country is not asked for a canton.

acceptance_criteria.title: Who receives the country of residence
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: the answers are recorded
acceptance_criteria.then: the country is recorded for HR as part of the postal address, is used for the source tax decision (anyone living outside Switzerland is subject to source tax, whatever their nationality) and decides which canton is entered for the pension fund.

sections.title: First working day and insurance start date
sections.purpose: Ask the employee for the contractual first working day and derive the pension fund insurance start date from it.

stories.title: Employee confirms the first working day
stories.i_want: to enter and confirm my contractual first working day in the first step of the questionnaire ('About you')
stories.so_that: HR and the pension fund work with the date that actually applies, even when it moved after I signed the contract
stories.priority_reason: HR calls the first working day 'the number one thing' for the pension fund, and it moves often; a wrong date caused a wrong registration at the fund and weeks of fixing (Julia).

acceptance_criteria.title: The first working day is asked of every employee and is required
acceptance_criteria.given: any new employee fills in the onboarding questionnaire, wherever they live and whatever their nationality or civil status
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee is in step 1 'About you' (together with first name, last name and date of birth; there is no separate step for the first working day)
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked for their first working day and cannot submit the questionnaire without it. The date is recorded for HR (start of employment) and is used to derive the pension fund insurance start date. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: the step order follows the eight fixed steps of the questionnaire.

examples.name: Employee starting on the 1st of a month

acceptance_criteria.title: The first working day is the contractual start date, even on a weekend or public holiday
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's contract starts on a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee enters the first working day
acceptance_criteria.then: the contractual start date is accepted as entered and is not moved to the next working day. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: the first working day is always the contractual start date.

acceptance_criteria.title: Plausible first working day
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee enters a first working day
acceptance_criteria.when: the date is shown as a day, month and year (DD.MM.YYYY)
acceptance_criteria.then: the date is accepted only if it lies within one year after the questionnaire was sent to the employee; otherwise the employee is asked to correct it before continuing. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: the one-year limit is a build-time value.

acceptance_criteria.title: The employee confirms the date on submission and cannot change it afterwards
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered the first working day and reaches the summary page
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee confirms the summary and submits
acceptance_criteria.then: the first working day is part of the confirmed answers. Until submission the employee can go back and change it; after submission the questionnaire is read-only for the employee and only HR can change the date. The latest date always counts and no history of earlier dates is kept. How HR changes it is specified in the later HR-side spec.

stories.title: Derive the pension insurance start date from the first working day
stories.i_want: the insurance start date of every new employee to be derived from their first working day: the same day if it is the 1st of a month, otherwise the 1st of the following month
stories.so_that: every registration carries a correct insurance start date on the 1st of a month without the employee having to know the fund's rule
stories.priority_reason: The insurance start date is required on the fund's registration form; a wrong date led to an unfriendly letter from the fund and weeks of fixing.

acceptance_criteria.title: First working day on the 1st of a month: insurance starts that day
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's first working day is the 1st of a month
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the insurance start date
acceptance_criteria.then: the insurance start date is the first working day itself, also when that day is a weekend or public holiday. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: the insurance start date is derived from the contractual first working day only.

acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's first working day is not the 1st of a month
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the insurance start date
acceptance_criteria.then: the insurance start date is the 1st of the month after the first working day, including across a year end

examples.name: Starts on the 2nd of a month
Starts on the last day of the year

acceptance_criteria.title: The employee is not asked for the insurance start date
acceptance_criteria.given: any new employee fills in the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee goes through the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is never asked for an insurance start date; it is derived from the first working day and recorded for the pension fund registration as a date (DD.MM.YYYY) on the 1st of a month

stories.title: Re-derive the insurance start date when the first working day moves
stories.i_want: the insurance start date to be derived again from the latest first working day whenever that date changes
stories.so_that: the fund never keeps a stale insurance start date, as happened with Julia when her start moved to the 15th of March and the date was not updated
stories.priority_reason: A missed update caused a wrong date at the fund, an unfriendly letter and weeks of fixing (Julia).

acceptance_criteria.title: Change before submission
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered a first working day and has not yet submitted
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee goes back and enters a different first working day
acceptance_criteria.then: the insurance start date is derived from the new date only; the earlier date plays no role and is not kept

acceptance_criteria.when: the first working day is changed
acceptance_criteria.then: the insurance start date is derived again from the latest first working day by the same rule (1st of a month: that day; otherwise the 1st of the following month). sections.title: Civil status and spouse data
sections.purpose: Ask the civil status of every employee and the spouse's or partner's date of birth where the fund needs it, and convert the civil status to the pension fund's list and to the calculator's two groups.

stories.title: Ask every employee for their civil status
stories.i_want: to state my civil status once, choosing from a list that covers my real situation, including a registered partnership or a separation
stories.so_that: the pension fund can register me and the source tax tariff can be worked out without HR asking me again
stories.priority_reason: Civil status is a required field of the pension fund registration; without it the registration is blocked (F-pension_portal-8664f4). It also drives the source tax tariff.

acceptance_criteria.title: Civil status is asked of every employee, wherever they live
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee filling in the onboarding questionnaire, living in Switzerland or abroad
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach step 4 'Civil status and spouse' of the eight questionnaire steps
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio asks for their civil status, and an answer is required before the questionnaire can be submitted. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert: the step order follows the eight fixed steps (D-047).

examples.name: Daniel, registered partnership, living in Switzerland (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-3907fe)

acceptance_criteria.title: Civil status offers exactly six values
acceptance_criteria.given: the civil status question is shown
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee chooses an answer
acceptance_criteria.then: they choose exactly one of: Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed, Registered partnership, Separated. The first four use the wording of the pension fund's list; Registered partnership and Separated are added because they occur (Daniel is in a registered partnership) and the source tax calculator names them. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-003).

acceptance_criteria.title: Civil status is recorded for the pension fund and for source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered the civil status question and submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: the answers are recorded for HR
acceptance_criteria.then: the civil status is recorded as needed by the pension fund (its required 'Civil status' field, converted to the fund's list) and by source tax (the calculator's civil status group and the spouse exemption in HR's source tax rule). How the data is sent to each party is out of scope.

stories.title: Ask for the spouse's or registered partner's date of birth when the fund registers the employee as Married
stories.i_want: the date of birth of the spouse or registered partner of every employee I register as Married, and no spouse data for anyone else
stories.so_that: the registration is not blocked by the missing 'Spouse's date of birth' and no personal data is collected that I do not need
stories.priority_reason: The fund's portal blocks the registration of a Married employee when the spouse's date of birth is empty (F-pension_portal-c5ee15).

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's or partner's date of birth is asked only for married, registered-partner and separated employees
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered the civil status question in step 4
acceptance_criteria.when: their civil status is Married, Registered partnership or Separated
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio asks for the date of birth of their spouse or registered partner in the same step, and an answer is required. For Single, Divorced and Widowed it is not asked and no spouse data is recorded for the fund. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert: registered partners and separated employees are entered at the fund as Married and therefore need this date; divorced and widowed employees do not (D-003, D-004; HR did not know what the fund wants for registered partners, F-hr_transcript-f197d6).

acceptance_criteria.title: The date is given as a calendar date
acceptance_criteria.given: the spouse's or partner's date of birth is asked
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee enters it
acceptance_criteria.then: it is a date in the form DD.MM.YYYY, as the fund's field expects.

acceptance_criteria.title: An answer that no longer applies is not kept
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee entered a spouse's date of birth and then changed their civil status to Single, Divorced or Widowed
acceptance_criteria.when: they submit the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the spouse's date of birth is discarded and not recorded; if they change back before submitting, the date they entered is still there.

acceptance_criteria.title: The date is recorded for the pension fund
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered the spouse's or partner's date of birth and submitted
acceptance_criteria.when: the answers are recorded for HR
acceptance_criteria.then: the date is recorded as the fund's 'Spouse's date of birth' for an employee entered at the fund as Married.

stories.title: Answer the calculator's civil status question from the employee's civil status
stories.i_want: the employee's civil status placed in one of the calculator's two groups
stories.so_that: the tariff code follows the calculator's logic without asking the employee a second civil status question
stories.priority_reason: Lonio computes the full tariff code instead of HR (D-001); the civil status group is an input to the tariff letter.

acceptance_criteria.title: Civil status is converted to the calculator's two groups
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered the civil status question
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio works out the civil status group for source tax
acceptance_criteria.then: Married and Registered partnership give 'Married or registered partnership'; Single, Divorced, Widowed and Separated give 'Single, divorced, separated or widowed', exactly as the calculator groups them. Registered partners therefore count as married for source tax, including the spouse exemption in HR's source tax rule. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-003). The group is derived again whenever the civil status changes (D-037).

stories.title: Enter the civil status on the pension fund's list
stories.i_want: every employee's civil status as one of my four values: Single, Married, Divorced or Widowed
stories.so_that: I can register every employee, including registered partners and separated employees, whom my list does not name
stories.priority_reason: Civil status is a required fund field with a fixed list; a value outside it cannot be entered and blocks the registration (F-pension_portal-8664f4, F-pension_portal-3d1ae4).

acceptance_criteria.title: Civil status is converted to the fund's list
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered the civil status question
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio works out the civil status for the pension fund
acceptance_criteria.then: Single, Married, Divorced and Widowed are entered as they are; Registered partnership and Separated are entered as Married, together with the spouse's or partner's date of birth. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert: HR did not know how the fund handles a registered partnership, and the fund's list has no value for it or for separation (D-003, D-004). The result is derived again whenever the civil status changes (D-037).

sections.title: Who is subject to source tax
sections.purpose: Ask only what HR's rule needs (nationality, C permit, and the spouse's nationality, C permit and whether the spouse lives in Switzerland) to decide whether the employee is subject to source tax.

stories.title: Ask nationality and C permit only of employees living in Switzerland
stories.i_want: Lonio to ask an employee who lives in Switzerland for their nationality and, if they are not Swiss, only whether they hold a C permit
stories.so_that: I can tell whether the employee is subject to source tax without collecting nationality or permit data from people for whom it changes nothing (employees living abroad are always subject to source tax)
stories.priority_reason: Nationality and C permit decide source tax liability for everyone living in Switzerland; without them HR cannot tell who has to answer the source tax questions (F-hr_transcript-b84498).

acceptance_criteria.title: Nationality is required only from employees living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered the country of their home address in step 2 (the address that applies on the first working day)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches step 3 'Nationality and C permit'
acceptance_criteria.then: if the home address is in Switzerland, the nationality is asked and required; if the home address is in any other country, the nationality is not asked, because an employee living abroad is subject to source tax whatever their passport. The nationality is recorded for HR to decide source tax liability and whether the permit reminder applies.

acceptance_criteria.title: Allowed nationality answers and dual citizens
acceptance_criteria.given: the nationality is asked
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee chooses their nationality
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee chooses one country from the ISO 3166 country list (English names) or 'stateless'. Anyone with Swiss citizenship chooses Switzerland, even if they also hold another nationality, and counts as Swiss for source tax. Assumption (D-008, D-050) - to be verified by a domain expert.

acceptance_criteria.title: C permit question only for non-Swiss employees living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland and has given their nationality
acceptance_criteria.when: the nationality is not Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio asks 'Do you hold a C permit (permanent residence)?' with the answers yes or no, and an answer is required; Swiss employees and employees living abroad are not asked. The answer is recorded for HR to decide source tax liability (a C-permit holder is treated like a Swiss person).

acceptance_criteria.title: No other permit type is asked
acceptance_criteria.given: a non-Swiss employee living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers step 3
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio asks only whether they hold a C permit and never asks which permit type they hold (for example a B permit), because no receiving party needs any other permit type. Assumption (D-005) - to be verified by a domain expert.

acceptance_criteria.title: Nationality and C permit answers are discarded when the employee moves the home address abroad
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee entered a home address in Switzerland, answered nationality and C permit, then went back and changed the home address country to another country
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee submits the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the nationality and C permit answers are no longer asked and are not kept; until submission they may be kept so that switching back loses no input.

stories.title: Ask the spouse's nationality, C permit and residence only when they can exempt the employee
stories.i_want: Lonio to ask a married employee or registered partner about their spouse's or partner's nationality, C permit and whether the spouse lives in Switzerland, but only when these answers can change the source tax decision
stories.so_that: I no longer have to check the spouse exemption by hand and chase spouse details by email, and no spouse data is collected when it cannot matter
stories.priority_reason: HR checks this exemption by hand today and asks by email, which 'takes forever' (F-hr_transcript-a45422); a wrong answer means the wrong source tax decision.

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's nationality and whether the spouse lives in Switzerland are asked only when they can exempt the employee
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered home address country, nationality, C permit and civil status
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee lives in Switzerland, is not Swiss, has no C permit and is Married or in a Registered partnership
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio asks for the spouse's (or registered partner's) nationality and asks 'Does your spouse live in Switzerland?' (yes or no); both are required. In every other case (Swiss employee, C-permit holder, employee living abroad, or civil status Single, Divorced, Widowed or Separated) neither is asked, because the answer cannot change the source tax decision. Assumptions (D-003: registered partnership counts as married and separated as single for source tax; D-050: residence asked as yes/no) - to be verified by a domain expert.

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's C permit is asked only for a non-Swiss spouse
acceptance_criteria.given: the spouse's nationality is asked
acceptance_criteria.when: the spouse's nationality is not Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio asks whether the spouse (or registered partner) holds a C permit, yes or no, and an answer is required; for a Swiss spouse it is not asked. No other permit type of the spouse is asked. Assumption (D-005) - to be verified by a domain expert.

acceptance_criteria.given: the spouse questions are asked
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers them

Whether the spouse lives in Switzerland is answered yes or no ('here' in HR's wording means Switzerland). The answers are recorded for HR only to decide the spouse exemption from source tax. stories.title: Decide whether the employee is subject to source tax
stories.i_want: Lonio to decide from the answers whether the new employee is subject to source tax, following our consolidated rule
stories.so_that: I know up front who has to answer the source tax questions and who needs a tariff code, instead of working it out by hand

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees living abroad are always subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: the home address on the first working day is in any country other than Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides source tax liability
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is subject to source tax whatever their nationality or civil status (HR's consolidated rule, which replaces the first version 'all non-Swiss employees').

acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the nationality is Switzerland (including dual citizens with Swiss citizenship), or the employee is not Swiss but holds a C permit
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is not subject to source tax, whatever their civil status. Assumption (D-008: Swiss citizenship counts even with another nationality) - to be verified by a domain expert.

acceptance_criteria.title: Non-Swiss employees in Switzerland without a C permit and without a spouse exemption are subject
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland, is not Swiss and has no C permit
acceptance_criteria.when: the civil status is Single, Divorced, Widowed or Separated
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is subject to source tax; separated counts as single, so the spouse is not considered. Assumption (D-003) - to be verified by a domain expert.

acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is not subject to source tax only if the spouse lives in Switzerland and is Swiss or holds a C permit; if the spouse lives outside Switzerland, or is neither Swiss nor a C-permit holder, the employee is subject to source tax. acceptance_criteria.title: The decision is recorded for HR and always follows the latest answers
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio records whether the employee is subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.then: the result is recorded for HR as 'yes' or 'no' and decides whether the source tax questions are asked; it is derived again whenever an answer it depends on changes. If an HR change after submission makes a question apply that was never asked (for example the home address moves from abroad to Switzerland, so nationality was never answered), the result shows 'incomplete - HR must complete' until HR enters the missing answers; the questionnaire is not reopened for the employee. Assumptions (D-048, D-053) - to be verified by a domain expert. The HR screens for this belong to the later HR-side spec.

stories.title: Derive the calculator's residence from the home address country
stories.i_want: Lonio to take my residence for the source tax tariff from the home address I already entered instead of asking me again
stories.so_that: I answer each piece of information only once
stories.priority_reason: Avoids a duplicate question (G-01, G-08); the tariff code needs it, but it adds no new data.

acceptance_criteria.title: Residence for the tariff is derived, never asked again
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered the country of their home address (as on the first working day)
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio works out the residence for the tariff calculation
acceptance_criteria.then: the calculator's questions 'main residence in Switzerland?' and 'country of residence' are not asked; the residence is Switzerland, Germany or Liechtenstein for those countries and 'Other country' for every other country. Switzerland and other countries lead to the base tariff without further residence questions; Germany and Liechtenstein lead to the cross-border questions. Assumption (D-041: the address that applies on the first working day) - to be verified by a domain expert. Unexplored calculator paths are checked before go-live (see OQ-calculator-coverage).

sections.title: Source tax: residence abroad and cross-border questions
sections.purpose: For employees living in Germany or Liechtenstein, ask the cross-border questions to decide between the cross-border tariff, the normal tariff and 'in principle no source tax liability' for Liechtenstein, including the separate note on the double taxation agreement.

stories.title: Derive the calculator's residence answers from the home address and ask cross-border questions only of Germany and Liechtenstein residents
stories.i_want: Lonio to take my country of residence from the home address I already gave, and to ask me cross-border questions only if I live in Germany or Liechtenstein
stories.so_that: I do not answer the same question twice or answer questions that do not apply to me, while Lonio still has everything it needs to compute my source tax tariff code
stories.priority_reason: Lonio computes the full tariff code itself (D-001); without the residence answers the tariff code for employees living abroad cannot be computed. HR today does not know up front who must answer which questions (F-hr_transcript-b84498, F-hr_transcript-8595fb).

acceptance_criteria.title: Residence for the tariff calculation is derived, not asked
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered the country of their home address as it applies on the first working day (step 2 Home address)
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio determines the residence for the source tax tariff calculation
acceptance_criteria.then: the calculator's questions 'main residence in Switzerland?' and 'country of residence' are not asked again; the residence is Switzerland for Switzerland, Germany for Germany, Liechtenstein for Liechtenstein, and 'Other country' for any other country. Switzerland and 'Other country' lead to the base tariff without further residence questions. This derivation is inferred from the calculator's options and is covered by the go-live check of the computed tariff code (see OQ-calculator-coverage).

acceptance_criteria.title: Cross-border questions only for Germany and Liechtenstein residents
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches step 5 Cross-border commuting
acceptance_criteria.then: an employee living in Germany is asked whether they return daily to their main residence in Germany; an employee living in Liechtenstein is asked whether they return daily to their main residence in Liechtenstein; an employee living in Switzerland or any other country is asked no cross-border question and step 5 is skipped. Employees living in Germany or Liechtenstein are always subject to source tax, as everyone living abroad is.

acceptance_criteria.title: Cross-border answers that no longer apply are discarded
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered cross-border questions for Germany or Liechtenstein and then changes the home address country to another country before submitting
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee submits the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the cross-border answers that no longer apply are discarded and not recorded; until submission they are kept, so that switching back restores them without retyping

stories.title: Germany: daily return and certificate of residence
stories.i_want: employees living in Germany to state whether they return home daily and, if so, whether they have a certificate of residence
stories.so_that: the cross-border tariff is applied only when the calculator's conditions are met and the normal tariff otherwise
stories.priority_reason: The answer changes the tariff letter (e.g. N1Y instead of C1Y); Lonio owns the tariff code (D-001) and HR could never remember the German forms (F-hr_transcript-8595fb).

acceptance_criteria.title: Daily return to Germany is asked of Germany residents
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Germany
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches step 5 Cross-border commuting
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked whether they return daily to their main residence in Germany, as they expect it for the year; the answer is required and is 'yes' or 'no'. It is recorded for the source tax tariff code. Employees living elsewhere are not asked.

acceptance_criteria.title: Certificate of residence is asked only with daily return
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Germany
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers that they return daily
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked whether they have a certificate of residence for HR; the answer is required and is 'yes', 'no' or 'not yet'. A new hire often has no certificate yet, so 'not yet' is valid. Nothing is uploaded: the document goes to HR outside Lonio. Employees who do not return daily are not asked.

acceptance_criteria.title: Cross-border tariff with daily return and certificate
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Germany and returns daily
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides between the cross-border and the normal tariff

stories.so_that: the child is counted, counted with tariff H or not counted exactly as the Zurich calculator does
stories.priority_reason: A wrong per-child result gives a wrong tariff letter or child digit; Lonio now owns the tariff result (D-001, D-009).

acceptance_criteria.title: Questions for a minor child in the household
acceptance_criteria.given: a child block with age status 'Minor' and 'yes' to living in the employee's household
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee continues in that block
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must state the parental custody: 'Shared custody' or 'Sole custody'. With shared custody, the employee must answer whether they live in a common household with the child's other parent (yes/no). Without a common household, the employee must answer whether there is alternating custody (yes/no). The main financial contributor ('Myself' or 'Other parent') is asked when there is alternating custody, and for single, divorced, separated or widowed employees who live in a common household with the other parent; married employees and registered partners in a common household are not asked it. For this, Married and Registered partnership form one group and Single, Divorced, Widowed and Separated the other, as in the calculator (assumption D-003, to be verified by a domain expert).

acceptance_criteria.title: Per-child result for a minor child in the household
acceptance_criteria.given: a completed block for a minor child living in the employee's household
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio works out the per-child result
acceptance_criteria.then: the result follows the calculator: sole custody counts the child (with tariff H for single, divorced, separated or widowed employees); shared custody with a common household counts the child for married employees and registered partners, and for the other group only if the employee is the main contributor (then with H); without a common household and with alternating custody the child counts only if the employee is the main contributor (with H for the single group); without alternating custody the child does not count for married employees and registered partners and counts with H for the single group. Observed calculator results win over the general rule (assumption D-046, to be verified by a domain expert); results marked inferred are compared with the calculator before go-live (D-009, see OQ-calculator-coverage).

acceptance_criteria.title: Questions for a minor child outside the household
acceptance_criteria.given: a child block with age status 'Minor' and 'no' to living in the employee's household
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee continues in that block
acceptance_criteria.then: married employees and registered partners must answer whether custody is shared (yes/no); single, divorced, separated and widowed employees must answer whether they have parental care (yes/no) - each group gets only its own question (grouping per assumption D-003, to be verified by a domain expert). With 'yes', the employee must answer whether there is alternating custody (yes/no), and with alternating custody, who makes the larger financial contribution ('Myself' or 'Other parent'). With 'no', the block ends.

acceptance_criteria.title: Questions for an adult child in first education
acceptance_criteria.given: a child block with age status 'Adult in first education'
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee continues in that block
acceptance_criteria.then: if the child lives in the household, the employee must answer whether they live in a common household with the child's other parent (yes/no). With a common household, single, divorced, separated and widowed employees must say who makes the larger financial contribution ('Myself' or 'Other parent'); married employees and registered partners are not asked anything more. If the child does not live in the household, or lives there without a common household with the other parent, the employee must answer whether they mainly (more than 50%) provide for the child's maintenance (yes/no). Grouping of civil statuses per assumption D-003, to be verified by a domain expert.

acceptance_criteria.title: Child digit is the number of counted children
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee for whom a tariff code is computed
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio computes the child digit
acceptance_criteria.then: the digit is the number of children whose result is 'counted' or 'counted with H', added up over all child blocks (for example three counted children give C3Y); a 'not counted' child adds nothing; without children the digit is 0. There is no maximum number of children (assumption D-044, to be verified by a domain expert); results with more than 3 children are checked against the calculator before go-live (D-009, see OQ-calculator-coverage). flow.intro: The questionnaire has eight steps, always in this order. Only the questions that apply to this employee are shown, and a step with no applicable question is skipped (for example step 3 for employees living abroad, steps 5 to 7 for employees who are not subject to source tax). Earlier answers decide which later questions apply, so basic facts come first, then residence, nationality, civil status, cross-border commuting, source tax details and children. Each answer is asked once and reused for every receiving party. Answers are saved as the employee goes and can be resumed until submission.

steps.title: About you
steps.asks: First name, last name, date of birth and first working day.

steps.title: Home address
steps.asks: Street, house number, postcode, town and country of residence as on the first working day; the canton only if the country is Switzerland.

steps.title: Nationality and C permit
steps.asks: Nationality; whether the employee holds a C permit only if not Swiss.

steps.title: Civil status and spouse
steps.asks: Civil status; the spouse's or partner's date of birth if married, in a registered partnership or separated; if the employee lives in Switzerland, is not Swiss, has no C permit and is married or in a registered partnership: the spouse's nationality, whether the spouse holds a C permit (if not Swiss) and whether the spouse lives in Switzerland.
steps.shown_to: Everyone (spouse questions only where the conditions apply)

steps.title: Cross-border commuting
steps.asks: Liechtenstein: daily return, and if not daily, whether more than 45 non-return days are expected. Germany: daily return; if daily, whether a certificate of residence exists ('not yet' counts as no); if not daily, whether daily return is reasonable and, if so, whether more than 60 non-return days are expected.
steps.shown_to: Employees living in Liechtenstein or Germany who are subject to source tax

steps.title: Source tax details
steps.asks: Denomination; whether the spouse or partner is gainfully employed (only if married or in a registered partnership); whether the employee has children.
steps.shown_to: Employees subject to source tax, except Liechtenstein residents who are in principle not liable

steps.title: Children
steps.asks: One block per child: whether the child is a minor or an adult in first education, whether the child lives in the household, and the follow-up questions on custody, parental care, common household with the other parent, alternating custody, main financial contributor and more than 50% maintenance, as far as they apply to that child.
steps.shown_to: Employees subject to source tax who have children

steps.title: Permit reminder, summary and submission
steps.asks: Nothing new is asked. The employee sees the permit reminder if it applies, reviews a summary of the answers and submits with one confirmation.
steps.shown_to: Everyone (the permit reminder only to non-Swiss employees living in Switzerland and to employees living abroad)

flow.closing: After submission the questionnaire is read-only for the employee and is never reopened. Answers that no longer apply are discarded on submission. Later changes are made by HR.
